findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector observed Medium-risk food class behaviors (hot holding) during today’s inspection. None of the staff at today’s inspection were Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPMs). Class II facilities must have a CFPM present to oversee proper food handling practices and temperatures for ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure a CFPM is present at all times during which food is being handled or hot held to mitigate the risk foodborne illnesses.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: No employee reporting agreements were available at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- all staff who were present signed the Employee Reporting Agreements. Ensure Employee Reporting Agreements are signed by all staff and maintained on file for future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an opened package of hotdogs (used for roller dogs) unlabeled and stored in the standing retail cooler. CORRECTED- package was moved to a cooler in the back of the store. Open packages of food for the public allow for a risk of contamination and adulteration. Cease this practice.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
All Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) items in the facility’s open air cooler were observed to contain an ambient temperature of 52F, and have internal temperatures between 46-53F. The PIC stated that the items had been in the cold holding unit for over 4 hours. CORRECTED: the following items were TCS OR labeled as “Keep Refrigerated”, and voluntarily removed from service, to be returned to the food supplier:
Cookie dough (X12), Chobani yogurt( X4), Pudding cups (X4), Sub sandwiches (X5), fruit cups (X3), grilled cheese sandwiches (X12), Italian wraps (X2), beef and cheddar sticks (X22), cheddar and salami sticks (X10), cheddar cheese curds (X3), Colby jack string cheese (X20), mozzarella and salami (X7), pepperoni and mozzarella (X7), mozzarella string cheese (X13), chocolate cake (X5), pickles (X12), banana cake (X8), strawberry cake (X5), birthday cake (X9), carrot cake (X4).
Ensure all TCS foods (as well as foods labeled “Keep Refrigerated”) are stored in cooling units that are at or below 41F. Inspector will do a spot check and bring temperature logs to maintain once the open air cooler is observed at or below 41F. Until that time utilize standing retail coolers for TCS foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The open air cooler was observed holding TCS foods between 46-53F. The unit contained a stem thermometer to monitor ambient temperatures, which initially read at 52F. During today’s inspection a myriad of TCS foods had to be discarded (see violation #22), and the open air cooler was unplugged and turned back on. The temperature of the unit was observed to be going down, but ensure the unit has either been serviced, or observed be able to hold foods at or below 41F before putting TCS foods back into this unit. The inspector will return by 12/22/25 to check the cold holding temperatures of this unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The facility’s stem thermometer was observed to be 8F higher than the inspector’s thermometer. CORRECTED- Education was provided and all stem thermometers were calibrated using the ice water method. Ensure all cold holding units contain accurate thermometers to monitor temperatures for food safety.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The drink divider racks in the facilities cooler were observed to contain an accumulation of mold. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of any soil debris. Inspector and the PIC discussed rotating which racks get deep cleaned on a regular basis. Deep clean these nonfood contact surfaces by the next routine inspection.
* This violation was noted as #55 at the pre-opening, and has since been reclassified.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The faucets at the facility’s triple sink were observed to be leaking. Ensure all plumbing is repaired by a licensed plumber 
* This violation was noted as #55 at the pre-opening, and has since been reclassified.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The following physical facilities noted during the pre-opening are still in need of repair:
-Replace wood shelves over the 3 compartment sink with something smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.
-Eliminate tape in the mop sink. Fill holes in the wall.
Physical facilities should be made to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
None of the staff were able to produce a Food Handler’s certificate during today’s inspection. Ensure all staff take an ANSI-approved Food Handler course, and print to maintain on file for future inspections. Inspector will provide a list of courses to the PIC when returning on 12/22. Ensure all staff members, and new staff obtain a Food Handler’s license within 30 days of hire.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]
